packageRules.description: Upper bounds on pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides are decisions, not drift: cross-major proposals wait under Pending Approval instead of opening a branch. Routine majors only; CONTRIBUTING.md explains the CI step that covers the rest.

Hold wasm-bindgen and js-sys in packages/cachekit-core-wasm. Both are exact-pinned, and scripts/build.sh fails unless the wasm-bindgen CLI equals the locked wasm-bindgen. Every CI workflow installs the CLI version Cargo.lock locks through .github/actions/setup-wasm-tools, the one place each version's SHA-256 is recorded, and refuses a version with none, so a bump moves the two pins and Cargo.lock together by hand and adds the new version's SHA-256 there. An update to either crate alone fails the Cargo.lock update, because js-sys pins wasm-bindgen exactly, and both together still fail CI until that SHA-256 is recorded, so it waits under Pending Approval on the Dependency Dashboard instead. Vulnerability updates are not held.

napi, napi-derive and napi-build update in their own napi-rs group, out of all-minor-patch. napi-rs releases napi, napi-derive and napi-derive-backend together, and a new napi-derive-backend can generate calls that only the napi released with it provides. minimumReleaseAge holds napi back for five days, but Cargo.lock takes the newest napi-derive-backend at once because it is transitive, so for up to five days after such a release the pair does not build: napi-derive-backend 6.1.6 calls napi::bindgen_prelude::defer_native_borrow_scope, which napi 3.14.2 lacks, and cachekit-core-ts failed with E0425. In its own group that window fails only the napi-rs PR, and the first Renovate run after napi clears the release age brings the matching napi. Majors group too, on their own branch, since napi-derive generates code for the napi of the same release.
